# Report a violation.
Illinois Condominium Violation Report, pursuant to Section 35 of the Condominium and Common Interest Community Ombudsperson Act (765 ILCS 615/35).

**Emergency?** Do not use this form. For flooding, fire, a gas smell, or an elevator entrapment, call [773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652). If anyone is in danger, call 911 first.

## Illinois Condominium Violation Report.
Pursuant to Section 35 of the Ombudsperson Act. This form is for reporting potential violations in condominium and common interest community properties under Illinois law. For emergencies, call 911. If you have photos, attach them to the email that opens.

- **[773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652)** Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM

- **[service@centerpointmgmt.com](mailto:service@centerpointmgmt.com)** Replies within one business day

- **5107 N Western Ave, Suite 1S** Chicago, IL 60625

## Why this form exists.
Illinois requires every condominium and common interest community association to have a written policy for resolving complaints from unit owners. Section 35 of the Condominium and Common Interest Community Ombudsperson Act (765 ILCS 615/35) says that policy must include a form owners can use to make a complaint, the address where complaints are sent, and reasonable time frames for the association to respond and to reach a final decision. This report is that form for the associations CenterPoint manages.

Because the requirement comes from state law, the form follows the same structure for every association: who is reporting, who is involved, what rule was broken, what happened, and what you are asking the board to do. Your association's declaration, bylaws, and rules decide what counts as a violation and what the board can do about it.

## Violation reporting and resolution.
Community standards only work when rules are enforced consistently and fairly. A written report gives the board a clear record of the concern, lets management investigate it properly, and protects the rights of every owner, including the owner the report is about. Every report is handled under the Illinois Condominium Property Act and your association's governing documents.

### Common violations.

- Noise disturbances and quiet hours violations
- Unauthorized modifications to units or common areas
- Parking and vehicle violations
- Pet policy violations
- Improper waste disposal
- Smoking in prohibited areas
- Unauthorized subletting or short-term rentals such as Airbnb
- Balcony and patio rule violations

### How a report is investigated.
Management logs the report, gathers evidence such as photos and witness statements, reviews the rule that applies, and contacts the people involved for their side. The goal is to resolve the issue through communication and cooperation before formal enforcement is needed.

### Fair enforcement and due process.
Under Section 18.4(l) of the Illinois Condominium Property Act (765 ILCS 605/18.4), the board can levy a fine only after the owner receives notice and an opportunity to be heard. In practice that means written notice of the alleged violation, a chance to respond or correct it, a hearing before the board if requested, and enforcement that moves from warnings to fines. Every step is documented, and the same rules apply to every owner.

### Illinois Ombudsperson Act information.
The Condominium and Common Interest Community Ombudsperson Act (765 ILCS 615/) gives unit owners a way to report potential violations of the Condominium Property Act or the Common Interest Community Association Act. For more information, or to contact the state directly, visit the [Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation](https://idfpr.illinois.gov/).

Read more about [how we manage violations](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/services/violation-management) and the [most common condo rule violations in Chicago](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/blog/common-condo-rule-violations-chicago).

## Common questions.

### Why does Illinois require a violation report form?
Section 35 of the Condominium and Common Interest Community Ombudsperson Act (765 ILCS 615/35) requires associations to adopt a written complaint policy that includes a form owners can use, where to send it, and reasonable time frames to respond and decide.

### Can I be fined because of a report?
Not without due process. Under 765 ILCS 605/18.4(l), the board must give the owner notice and an opportunity to be heard before levying a fine.

### Will the owner I report know it was me?
The report may be shared with the board and others involved in the investigation, as the acknowledgement on the form explains. If you are worried about how your report will be handled, say so in the details or call our office before you send it.

### What if the problem is happening right now?
For ongoing noise or disturbances, call our office at [773.728.0652](tel:+17737280652) during business hours. For anything dangerous or illegal, call 911.

### Can I report a common area that needs repair?
Use the [maintenance request form](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/resources/maintenance-request). Repairs are handled faster as work orders than as violation reports.
